title: Promptset coverage + failure triage synthesis (Mar 1–13, 2026)
content:
TL;DR:
- Coverage heatmap indicates 8 prompt families with <60% example coverage across model variants (see coverage snapshot section).
- Net quality delta (primary onboarding metric: pass-rate@threshold) fell from 82.1% (baseline) to 77.0% = -5.1pp over the last two weeks for models entering staging.
- Hallucination-like failures rose from 2.3% -> 4.1% for open-answer tasks; top correlated triggers: long instruction concatenation and numerical reasoning prompts.
- Immediate recommended actions: (1) prioritize gap-filling for three prompt families (NLP-cleaning, invoice-parse, policy-redaction), (2) add targeted canonicalization preprocessor for numeric/date tokens, (3) schedule a small canary rollout with caching disabled to validate model fallback behavior.

Background/context:
This synthesis pulls together promptset coverage, run-level regression snapshots, and the triage for top failure archetypes observed across onboarding runs for the last two weeks (Mar 1–13, 2026). Primary audience: applied-ml onboarding owners, model infra, and product owners responsible for model quality gates.

What we measured (quick):
- Primary metric: pass-rate@threshold (binary eval per prompt expected output rule).
- Secondary metrics: hallucination-rate (model produces unsupported claims), format-failure-rate (structural parsing errors), latency P95, and token-usage delta vs baseline.
- Dataset: 14 onboarding prompt families (contains ~12k examples total); runs across model variants v1.0, v1.1-quant, and v2-lite.

Coverage snapshot (summary):
- Prompt families with poorest coverage (examples covered by unit tests or canonical asserts):
  * invoice-parse: 42% coverage — many edge-case dates and currency codes missing
  * policy-redaction: 38% coverage — insufficient named-entity masked examples
  * nl-cleaning: 51% coverage — lacks noisy-web-corpus variants
  * multi-hop-reference: 55% coverage — long-context cross-ref cases sparse
- Heatmap note: coverage gaps concentrated on numeric canonicalization, parentheses/bracket-heavy inputs, and multi-locale date formats.

Regression deltas (aggregate):
- pass-rate@threshold: baseline 82.1% -> current 77.0% (-5.1pp)
- hallucination-rate (open answers): 2.3% -> 4.1% (+1.8pp)
- format-failure-rate: 6.7% -> 8.4% (+1.7pp)
- average token usage per response: +4.2 tokens (+3.4%)
- latency P95: 320ms -> 340ms (+20ms)
Note: Most of the pass-rate regression concentrated in three prompt families (invoice-parse, policy-redaction, numeric-reasoning).

Top failure archetypes (ranked) + examples + quick mitigations:
1) Numeric canonicalization mismatch (est. 31% of failures)
   - Example: expected "USD 1,200" -> model outputs "1200 dollars", downstream parser flags as mismatch.
   - Likely cause: tokenization/quantization changes in v1.1-quant and lack of normalization in test assertions.
   - Quick fix: add canonicalization pre-step in eval harness + normalize both golden and predicted before assert. Owner: Liang Z. (JIRA-ML-4187). Effort: 1 engineer, 1 day.

2) Partial redaction misses (policy-redaction) (est. 24%)
   - Example: model returns partially redacted emails "j***@example.com" when spec requires full mask "[EMAIL]".
   - Likely cause: training distribution shift + ambiguous spec language in prompts.
   - Mitigation: strengthen negative examples, add explicit prompt templates that prefer fully masked tokens, and add unit tests that assert exact token for redaction. Owner: Sofia N. (JIRA-ML-4210). Effort: 2 days including new prompt examples.

3) Hallucinated numeric facts in long-instruction concatenations (est. 14%)
   - Example: asked to sum two numbers embedded in long user text; model invents different sum.
   - Cause: context window tokenization and attention sparsity on numeric tokens.
   - Mitigation: add focused few-shot exemplars for arithmetic in promptset; consider micro-finetune or chain-of-thought style prompt. Owner: Diego M. (JIRA-ML-4205). Effort: 3–5 days to evaluate.

4) Output formatting truncation on quantized variant (est. 12%)
   - Example: JSON output missing trailing fields. Observed more on v1.1-quant.
   - Mitigation: add deterministic end-of-output sentinel and assert presence of keys in harness; investigate runtime token clipping heuristics. Owner: infra-serving (ticket infra-879). Effort: infra + eval: 2 days.

5) Locale/date parsing failures (est. 9%)
   - Example: "03/04/2026" ambiguous between DD/MM and MM/DD in tests expecting DD/MM.
   - Mitigation: add locale-aware canonicalization; add locale annotation in prompt metadata. Owner: Applied ML. Effort: 1 engineer, 2 days.

Action items (concrete, prioritized):
- A1 (P0): Add canonicalization layer in eval harness and re-run full onboarding suite. Owner: Liang Zhao. ETA: 2026-03-16. Ticket: JIRA-ML-4187.
- A2 (P0): Implement and add 400 targeted examples for policy-redaction family (edge cases, international names). Owner: Sofia Nguyen. ETA: 2026-03-20. Ticket: JIRA-ML-4210.
- A3 (P1): Run a canary of v1.1-quant with caching disabled on staging to isolate runtime-induced truncation. Owner: infra-serving + Diego M. ETA: 2026-03-17. Ticket: infra-879.
- A4 (P1): Create three numeric-reasoning few-shot templates and evaluate impact on pass-rate (A/B). Owner: Diego Morales. ETA: 2026-03-18. Ticket: JIRA-ML-4205.
- A5 (P2): Expand promptset coverage for multi-locale dates and currency (add ~250 examples). Owner: Applied ML interns. ETA: 2026-03-25.

Risk and rollback guidance:
- If pass-rate does not recover >= +3pp after canonicalization + redaction fixes, block promotion of v1.1-quant to dedicated until further analysis.
- Canary rollout should include a fallback to v1.0 and automated traffic shift if format-failure-rate exceeds 10% in first 1 hour.

Experiment notes / open hypotheses (for records):
- H1: Quantization variant is amplifying tokenization edge cases leading to format truncation. Test: compare decode logits on failing examples between v1.0 and v1.1-quant. Owner: inference-research.
- H2: Increased hallucination in long concatenations arises from new training examples that include rhetorical/informal language. Test: measure pass-rate by prompt length bucket.

Quick dashboard pointers (how to reproduce the key charts):
- Run: eval-scripts/run_onboard_suite.sh --since 2026-03-01 --to 2026-03-13 --models v1.0,v1.1-quant,v2-lite --output ./reports/mar1-13
- Coverage heatmap: reports/mar1-13/coverage/heatmap.csv -> pivot by prompt_family vs clause_type.
- Failure archetype extraction: reports/mar1-13/failures/archetype_counts.csv (script: scripts/cluster_failures.py --min-cluster-size 5)

Appendix: per-promptset delta highlights (short list)
- invoice-parse: pass-rate -9.8pp, format-failure +4.0pp. Key missing cases: negative amounts, EUR with comma decimals.
- policy-redaction: pass-rate -7.2pp, hallucination +1.1pp. Key missing cases: partial matches, embedded emails in URLs.
- numeric-reasoning: pass-rate -4.5pp, hallucination +2.0pp.
- nl-cleaning: pass-rate -2.3pp (mostly unchanged), coverage gaps noted.

Notes-to-self / next steps for doc owner:
- Re-run the onboarding harness after canonicalizer patch and include side-by-side diff artifact in Confluence under "Onboarding diffs / Mar 2026".
- Schedule 30-min sync with infra-serving to discuss canary parameters.
- Follow up on JIRA tickets above and update this doc status to "in_review" when A1/A2 are merged.

References & artifacts:
- Promptset Registry (confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ML/Promptset+Registry
- Eval harness PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-scripts/pull/224
- Related tickets: JIRA-ML-4187, JIRA-ML-4205, JIRA-ML-4210, infra-879

End of synthesis.

(Informal notes: this doc mixes quick triage notes with suggested next experiments; keep iterative — will convert to a formal retro if post-fix runs show persistent regressions.)
